name: Luminarch Ascension
oracle_text:
At the beginning of each opponent's end step, if you didn't lose life this turn, you may put a quest counter on this enchantment. (Damage causes loss of life.)
{1}{W}: Create a 4/4 white Angel creature token with flying. Activate only if this enchantment has four or more quest counters on it.
blocked_sentences: {1}{W}: Create a 4/4 white Angel creature token with flying. Activate only if this enchantment has four or more quest counters on it.

needs.what: A token id for a 4/4 white Angel creature token with flying -- flying only, no vigilance. Suggested id `angel_4_4_w_flying`, added to data/cards/tokens.cards.json next to the existing `angel_4_4_w_flying_vigilance` entry, with `types: ["Creature"]`, `subtypes: ["Angel"]`, `power: 4`, `toughness: 4`, `keywords: ["flying"]`, `colors: ["W"]`, `color_identity: ["W"]`, `is_token: true`. This is the plain Angel token printed by Luminarch Ascension, Entreat the Angels, Geist-Honored Monk, Angelic Accord and Requiem Angel, so it is not a one-card addition.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `token_ids` is a closed list and its only 4/4 white Angel is `angel_4_4_w_flying_vigilance` -- "4/4 white Angel creature with flying and vigilance" (data/cards/tokens.cards.json, the entry with keywords ["flying", "vigilance"]). Luminarch Ascension prints a 4/4 white Angel with flying and nothing else, so that token is a strictly better creature: it would attack without tapping, which changes combat maths on the exact card the token is the payoff for. The brief forbids substituting a nearly-right token, and no op builds a token from characteristics -- `create_token` names a pre-declared id, `copy_permanent` copies an existing permanent rather than minting from a printed description, and `animate`/`set_pt` operate on objects that already exist. So the only route is the data entry.
